problems.statement: Riverside's collapse (ticket time 18 to 31 min, rating 4.6 to 4.0, comps tripled) is a localized staffing failure: loss of the saute/pasta cook on 2026-08-08, no replacement, and a single trainee covering Fri/Sat dinners, with group operations deferring transfer requests.
Group kitchens are broadly inefficient (19 min vs 12 min benchmark) and need standardizing on par-cooked/frozen components.

The 17-18 minute ticket time at the eight non-Riverside locations is a deliberate, board-accepted consequence of the October 2024 'Made Here' redesign, not an execution failure; it came with higher food quality, price/check and sales growth.
The Pellston 12-minute benchmark is not comparable, because the panel required at least 60% pre-prepared or frozen components, excluded scratch kitchens, and had lower check averages.

The 19.1 group average is a composite artifact: Riverside's Aug-Sep spike lifts a stable 17.6 average, and Pellston's window (Aug-Sep 2026) coincides with Riverside's problem and was not broken down by location or earlier period.
Slow service is a group-wide guest problem that drives dissatisfaction and will spread from Riverside to the other locations.

Speed of service was always the lowest-rated attribute and is unchanged at 4.1 to 4.2; overall satisfaction and repeat visits rose after the redesign, though the repeat-visit rise is confounded by a measurement change and a rewards app launch.
Riverside GM Tom Kessler's own conduct caused the cook's departure (the Sunday-hours cut was a leadership failure) and he needs replacing.

The Sunday-hour cut was a group-standard-compliant response to the bridge-closure cover drop (the other line cooks were cut equally), so it is unlikely to be the sole reason for Delgado's resignation; his reason (relocation vs grievance) is unresolved.
Group operations' deferral of transfer cook requests 'pending ownership staffing review' is the main organizational mechanism that turned a single vacancy into a prolonged service failure.
Tying GM bonuses to a 12-minute ticket-time target would be counterproductive: it is unreachable under the current menu, and self-reported KDS bump data was previously gamed.

actions.action: Immediately fill Riverside's saute/pasta capacity by transferring or lending an experienced cook from another location, and fast-track the open requisition.
actions.rationale: The KDS shows 71% of the Riverside increase sits at the saute/pasta station, and no other location has had a line vacancy open longer than three weeks, so the fix is simple and fast.

actions.action: Have group operations lift the 'pending staffing review' deferral and set a rule that line vacancies are covered within a defined number of days.
actions.rationale: The deferral policy is the organizational cause that kept a one-cook gap open for more than three months.

actions.action: Re-forecast Riverside line hours for the bridge closure while protecting Friday and Saturday peak coverage.
actions.rationale: Sunday cuts followed the group labor standard, but peak-night staffing is now the binding constraint.

actions.action: Run a structured exit and retention check with Delgado (if reachable) and the Riverside line cooks to establish why he left.
actions.rationale: The accounts conflict and the exit interview was not completed, so the reason matters for retention but does not change the immediate fix.

actions.action: Standardize all nine kitchens on par-cooked/frozen components as Pellston recommends.
actions.rationale: The benchmark is not comparable, the group average is inflated by Riverside, the 2024 trial showed quality and brand loss, and the Made Here positioning is tied to higher check and same-store sales growth.

actions.action: Write a 12-minute ticket-time target into every GM's bonus from Q1 2027.
actions.rationale: The target is unreachable under the current menu, and the 2023 audit showed self-reported KDS times get bumped early without any real speed gain.

actions.action: Replace Riverside's GM Tom Kessler now.
actions.rationale: The evidence points to a staffing gap and an ownership deferral rather than a leadership failure, and the Delgado causation is disputed and secondhand.

actions.action: Rebase the performance review on a like-for-like benchmark (scratch or made-to-order peers), with location-level data, and decide with the board whether the 19-minute ceiling and the trade-off still hold.
actions.rationale: This tests the owner's real question about efficiency using a valid comparison rather than a mismatched panel.

actions.action: Monitor Riverside weekly (ticket time by station, rating, comps) and the other eight locations for spillover.
actions.rationale: This confirms recovery after the staffing fix and catches any generalization of the problem.

nextEvidence: Why Delgado left (a cook interview or outreach, plus any documented complaints), and whether other Riverside cooks are at risk.
Ticket time and satisfaction at made-to-order or scratch-kitchen peers, to give a valid benchmark and show where Copperleaf's 17-18 minutes sits.
Riverside weekly KDS station times and ratings after cover is restored, to confirm the cook shortage explains the whole spike (not a second cause).
output.summary: The 'kitchens are inefficient' premise does not hold. Eight locations have run a stable 17.6 minutes since the board knowingly traded about 4 extra minutes for the October 2024 made-to-order menu, and that menu came with higher food quality, check and same-store sales. Pellston's 12-minute benchmark excludes scratch kitchens. The 19.1 average is inflated by Riverside, whose spike traces to losing its saute/pasta cook in August, no replacement, and group operations deferring transfer requests. Do not go frozen or add a 12-minute GM bonus (a past audit showed ticket-time bonuses were gamed). Fix Riverside's staffing now. Do not replace the GM on current evidence.
